messages:
incident-bot: PAGE: SLO alert — streaming p99 > 5s for customer FjordAI in us-west-2. Impacting streaming sessions and increasing timeouts. Paging on-call. :rotating_light:

jason_oncall: acked, I'm on it. pulling metrics now. what's the customer footprint?

maya_sre: FjordAI is single-tenant on hosted; spike started ~7250001200. p95 jumped from ~140ms -> ~1.8s, p99 ~5.9s. streaming stall rate from 2.3% -> 16%.

raj_ml: FYI they've started sending significantly longer prefixes earlier today — nested system prompts + chunked user docs. Could be KV cache thrash.

tina_cs: FjordAI support reporting: "chat sessions hang for several seconds, then partial stream, sometimes timeout around 10s". They have ~800 concurrent streaming req/s at peak (sustained for last 15m).

ben_eng: pulling logs for serving pool that handles fjordai. seeing repeated kvcache.eviction logs and token_delay_ms spikes. snippet:```
[7250001221] INFO kvcache: eviction_count=1324 evict_rate=0.82
[7250001222] WARN runtime: token_delay_ms=4123 sess=abcd1234 model=rdm-3b
[7250001224] ERROR stream: stall detected sess=abcd1234 reason=kv_miss
```

alice_pm: is this concentrated to one model variant or across model family? any recent deploys?

raj_ml: looks concentrated on rdm-3b and rdm-6b families with long-prefix optimization paths. Smaller rdm-lite unaffected. No recent model deploys in last 6h (checked deploy logs).

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline: no model changes in last 8h. Last infra deploy: 7250000100 infra-agent v2.3.1 -> v2.3.1 (noop).

maya_sre: quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle tenant concurrency 2) route FjordAI traffic to dedicated pool with larger KV cache, 3) fallback to rdm-lite for streaming if needed. Can we apply concurrency throttle now?

jason_oncall: do it. throttle to 6 concurrent streams per-tenant for FjordAI. Ben, can you run the routing change?

ben_eng: applying throttle via admin route:```bash
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/tenants/fjordai/config -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' -d '{"max_concurrent_streams":6}'
```
applied.

ben_eng: now flipping routing policy to dedicated pool (pool-id:d-pool-west-large). config snippet:```json
{"route":"tenant:ffjordai","pool":"d-pool-west-large","policy":"prefer_dedicated","drain_seconds":30}```
curl -X POST https://admin.internal/api/routes -d @route.json -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'

ben_eng: route changed; traffic will gradually shift. monitoring p95/p99.

maya_sre: also setting an automatic fallback to rdm-lite-v1 for streaming responses longer than 2048 tokens. config applied.

raj_ml: note: fallback reduces quality but removes the long-prefix optimized path that causes KV pressure. acceptable as temporary mitigation.

jason_oncall: running quick check: kubectl get pods -l pool=d-pool-west-large -o wide -> scaled to 12 nodes, CPU ~72%, GPU mem ~65%.

ben_eng: observed immediate effect: p95 -> 350ms, p99 -> 1.1s after routing shift (10m window). streaming stall rate down to 3.4%.

tina_cs: relaying to customer: "we routed your traffic to an isolated pool and temporarily throttled concurrency to protect sessions; you may see lower latency now, we're continuing to monitor." They asked for ETA to full restoration.

alice_pm: what's next for root cause? looks like workload pattern + KV cache sizing mismatch under sustained concurrency. need follow-up runbook.

raj_ml: agree. propose post-mortem actions: - increase default kv cache size for customers with nested prompts - add tenant-level adaptive prefetch / prefix coalescing - detect long-prefix fanout and auto-suggest model quantization or fallback - add dashboard alert for kvcache.eviction rate >= 0.5 over 5m

maya_sre: creating incident ticket: INC-7250001. assigning Raj/Ben/Maya/Jason for 72h RCA.

jason_oncall: handing off to night oncall @maya_sre. if regress, page with P1. otherwise we'll close after 4h stable window. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: NOTE: Please add timeline updates to INC-7250001 and tag with customer:fjordai.

ben_eng: quick commands I ran for traceability:```bash
# check stream stalls
kubectl logs -l app=redwood-serving -c serving --since=15m | grep stall | tail -n 50
# revert routing (if needed)
curl -X DELETE https://admin.internal/api/routes/<route-id> -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN'
```

tina_cs: customer confirms improved UX at 7250001295, no new timeouts observed in 10m sample. thanks team. :pray:

maya_sre: marking mitigation stable at 7250001305, will keep monitoring overnight. RCA follow-up meeting scheduled tomorrow 16:00 PT.

jason_oncall: great work everyone. closing live triage, handing to RCA squad. :rocket:
